# Python Tip: Starred Unpacking

Need to unpack a list?  
But don't know exactly how many values it contains?  
Use `*` to capture the flexible part!  

:::{.python-logo}
:::

:::

:::



<!-- PANEL 2 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## Variable-Length Data

Frequently in coding, we work with lists where the order of the elements has meaning, but the total length of the list can vary.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
# A file path can have any number of folders
path_parts = ["users", "ada", "docs", "report.txt"]

# A command can have any number of arguments
command_parts = ["copy", "report.txt", "backup/"]
```
:::

In `path_parts`, the last value is the filename, while the preceding values are the folders.

In `command_parts`, the first value is the command—the action to perform. The remaining values are the arguments it needs.

How can we easily parse these lists?

:::



<!-- PANEL 3 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## Don't Parse It by Hand

Indexing and slicing work, but they focus on positions instead of meaning.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
command_parts = ["copy", "report.txt", "backup/"]

command = command_parts[0]
arguments = command_parts[1:]

print("Command:", command)
print("Arguments:", arguments)
```
:::

Python gives us a clearer way to say, "the first value and everything else."

:::



<!-- PANEL 4 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## The Starred Unpacking Rule

Regular variables receive one value. A starred variable captures the remaining values in a list.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
command_parts = ["copy", "report.txt", "backup/"]

command, *arguments = command_parts

print("Command:", command)
print("Arguments:", arguments)
```
:::

The assignment now describes the meaning of the data directly.

:::



<!-- PANEL 5 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## The Star Can Move

For a file path, the filename is last while the number of folders can vary.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
path_parts = "users/ada/docs/report.txt".split("/")

*folders, filename = path_parts

print("Folders:", folders)
print("File:", filename)
```
:::

The starred variable captures the flexible beginning instead.

:::



<!-- PANEL 6 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

## Unpack Into Functions

We can also use `*` to unpack a list into a function call.

:::{.code-animation}
```{python}
def copy_file(source, destination):
    print(source, "->", destination)

command_parts = ["copy", "report.txt", "backup/"]
command, *arguments = command_parts

copy_file(*arguments)
```
:::

On the left of `=`, `*` gathers values. In a function call, it spreads them.

:::



<!-- PANEL 7 -->
:::{.tutorial-panel}

:::{.center}

## Wrap-Up

Use starred unpacking when positions have meaning, but part of a sequence can vary in length.

`command, *arguments` captures everything after the first value.

`*folders, filename` captures everything before the last value.

`function(*arguments)` spreads those values into a function call.
